claims.text: Introducing nanoscale SRO precipitates into an otherwise well-ordered insulating oxide will reduce phonon scattering times.
Reducing phonon scattering times through SRO precipitates will lower lattice thermal conductivity.
High-purity single-crystal α-Al2O3 can provide a nearly perfect, defect-free reference lattice.
Heat conduction in high-purity sapphire is dominated by phonons under the proposed conditions.
A minor transition-metal-oxide addition combined with tailored heat treatment can form nanoscale SRO precipitates in sapphire.
The proposed treatment will produce discrete nanoscale precipitates exhibiting chemical short-range order within the sapphire matrix.
SRO precipitates act as additional phonon-scattering centers.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces the effective phonon mean free path.
A reduced phonon mean free path decreases the lattice contribution to overall thermal conductivity.
SRO-precipitate-containing sapphire will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than pristine sapphire.
The expected reduction in lattice thermal conductivity is approximately 10–30%.
Pristine high-purity α-Al2O3 typically has a room-temperature lattice thermal conductivity of approximately 35 W/m·K.
The proposed effect is most relevant where phonon conduction dominates and electronic thermal conduction is negligible.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity change may vary with precipitate size, volume fraction, and spatial distribution.
The quantitative relationship between precipitate characteristics and phonon mean-free-path reduction is not precisely known.
